transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Elena Gomez (Redwood CSM); Jill Thompson (Acme Head of MLOps), Rajesh Kumar (CTO), Linda Park (Security Eng), Carlos Rivera (Platform Eng)

Summary: Kickoff for onboarding Acme Health to Redwood Inference hosted -> plan out SSO, data handling, dedicated pilot, and initial benchmarks. Discussed security requirements (SOC2/KMS/SSO), deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC), and next steps for pilot timeline.

Topics: Onboarding runbook, SSO/SAML, audit logs/KMS, pilot scope (benchmarks), pricing for dedicated capacity, timeline and stakeholders.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Sofia from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, and i'll kick us off. we are joined by Marcus our SE and Elena our CSM.
[00:00:12] Jill Thompson: Hey thanks, Jill here, excited to get started. we have a few folks from platform and security.
[00:00:18] Rajesh Kumar: Hi all, quick intro, i'm Rajesh, CTO at Acme Health, just want to make sure this rollout is secure and low-risk.
[00:00:25] Marcus Li: Great, hi team. i'll be leading the technical onboarding and benchmark work. a little preview: we'll want to align on sample workloads, SLOs for latency, and some security controls.
[00:00:35] Sofia Patel: Agenda for today: 1) confirm stakeholders and timeline, 2) go over onboarding runbook + SSO, 3) discuss pilot scope (hosted vs dedicated), 4) compliance requirements, 5) next steps.
[00:00:50] Carlos Rivera: timeline wise we are aiming for a pilot in ~4 weeks, internal sign-off in 8 weeks, so want to see what you need to hit those dates.
[00:01:01] Elena Gomez: Perfect, we typically structure a 4-week pilot with milestones: env setup & SSO, model selection and bench, integration tests, then go/no-go.
[00:01:12] Linda Park: From security: SOC2 is baseline, we also need audit logs retention, KMS integration for keys, and proof of data residency controls.
[00:01:25] Marcus Li: On the key mgmt: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for private deployments and Dedicated with KMS integration for hosted as well. In the pilot we can show logs and encryption in transit at minimum.
[00:01:40] Jill Thompson: good — also curious on data retention, is there any short term caching that could leak PHI? we need to be careful.
[00:01:48] Marcus Li: yes, good call. Redwood has prefix and KV cache mechanisms that can be configured; for PHI workloads we'd disable persistent KV caching or ensure it's encrypted with customer keys and strict TTLs. i'll capture the config options.
[00:02:05] Sofia Patel: Quick qualification: who will be the main integration owner? Carlos?
[00:02:09] Carlos Rivera: i'll be primary for platform integration, but Jill and Linda will own ML and security signoffs.
[00:02:17] Sofia Patel: Great. Pilot success criteria — what would make this a win for Acme?
[00:02:23] Jill Thompson: We need to validate latency under typical load (end-to-end 95th < 200ms for short prompts), cost per 1k tokens under our estimated throughput, and zero data leakage.
[00:02:36] Rajesh Kumar: Also operational tooling — traces, per-route cost breakdown, and ability to pin models for rollouts.
[00:02:44] Marcus Li: Noted. On latency targets: 200ms 95th is achievable for many lighter models on dedicated capacity but depends on prompt size and quantization. there's always the tradeoff: smaller model + quantization saves cost but might regress on quality.
[00:02:59] Linda Park: we need to see model evals for quality; can't sacrifice medical accuracy.
[00:03:05] Marcus Li: Agreed — we'll run evaluation sets you provide and compare quality across model variants.
[00:03:11] Sofia Patel: On deployment options: do we plan for Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPUs), or Private VPC/on-prem?
[00:03:20] Jill Thompson: For pilot hosted is fine if data controls and KMS meet our bar; long-term we might need Dedicated in a VPC for isolation.
[00:03:29] Rajesh Kumar: We prefer dedicated for production, but pilot can use hosted with strict KMS and audit controls.
[00:03:35] Marcus Li: That maps to typical path: hosted pilot -> Dedicated reserved capacity -> Private if required. We can show a canary rollout and fallback to smaller model if latency spikes.
[00:03:46] Carlos Rivera: about fallback — how is routing handled? we want predictable behavior under load.
[00:03:51] Marcus Li: Redwood does smart routing by policy: latency-first, cost-first, region-based. We can configure failover to a compatible variant and keep per-token tracing so you know what's served.
[00:04:05] Sofia Patel: Questions from our side: what's your expected QPS and typical prompt length?
[00:04:11] Jill Thompson: For peak - 40 concurrent requests with avg prompt 120 tokens, sometimes longer. Rough monthly tokens ~200M.
[00:04:21] Marcus Li: ok that volume maps to a mid-size dedicated pool. we'll size a pilot cluster to handle peaks with some headroom. Estimated cost we'll share after we run a small sim.
[00:04:34] Sofia Patel: Linda, any more on compliance?
[00:04:37] Linda Park: also need SSO, SAML, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC with audit trails, and retention periods for logs. can you provide the schema for audit logs?
[00:04:48] Marcus Li: yes, we can provide audit log schema. i'll attach the sample logs and retention options. for SSO we have SAML and OIDC support and SCIM for user sync.
[00:05:00] Rajesh Kumar: Do you have SOC 2 type 2?
[00:05:03] Elena Gomez: Redwood has SOC2 Type II; we'll send the compliance pack and redacted audit report under NDA if needed.
[00:05:12] Carlos Rivera: networking — for dedicated or private we need VPC peering or private link. what's the typical network setup?
[00:05:19] Marcus Li: For Dedicated we offer private endpoint options that sit in your VPC via PrivateLink or VPN. For on-prem it's a managed package. We'll share the network diagram.
[00:05:31] Jill Thompson: excellent. On the technical side, can we run an initial quality benchmark on a small dataset next week?
[00:05:37] Marcus Li: yes, please share a sanitized sample of your prompts and we will run a quality and latency benchmark. Prefer CSV with columns: prompt, expected_output, metric.
[00:05:50] Sofia Patel: i'll follow up with an email with the runbook and a link to the onboarding doc.
[00:05:55] Linda Park: regarding data residency — some of our data must stay in eu-west region; can Redwood pin region for the model?
[00:06:03] Marcus Li: yes, model routing can be region pinned; we can provision capacity in eu-west for those requests.
[00:06:10] Rajesh Kumar: Pricing question — dedicated vs hosted delta?
[00:06:14] Sofia Patel: we'll provide a dedicated pricing sheet; typically dedicated has a monthly commit plus lower per-token execution cost. we'll send a tailored estimate based on your token forecasts.
[00:06:25] Carlos Rivera: any notes about quantization impact on accuracy for medical prompts?
[00:06:30] Marcus Li: quantization helps latency and cost but can slightly affect quality; we'll test 4-bit/8-bit configurations and include evals. for critical outputs we recommend running regression tests and maybe using full precision for select routes.
[00:06:44] Jill Thompson: ok makes sense.
[00:06:47] Sofia Patel: let's map out the immediate next week: 1) share runbook and SSO docs (we'll send today), 2) Acme to provide sample prompts and success metrics by 10/17, 3) Marcus to run a bench and share results by 10/20, 4) security Qs from Linda by 10/18.
[00:07:05] Linda Park: i'll compile the compliance list, thanks.
[00:07:09] Marcus Li: i'll ask for access patterns and any traffic shaping rules you want to test.
[00:07:15] Sofia Patel: Any blockers from your side for the pilot timeline?
[00:07:19] Carlos Rivera: main blocker is procurement for pilot PO if dedicated tests required; otherwise hosted pilot fine.
[00:07:26] Rajesh Kumar: procurement will need an estimate — can you provide a pilot cost range?
[00:07:30] Sofia Patel: yes we'll include a pilot cost estimate in the follow-up.
[00:07:34] [15:00 cut — meeting continues with more detailed Q&A and technical clarifications]
[00:07:45] Marcus Li: quick technical note about caching: we have automatic prefix caching and request-level KV cache for repeated context, but for PHI we can disable or isolate caches and log cache usage.
[00:07:56] Jill Thompson: good, we'll need that disabled for the PHI endpoints.
[00:08:02] Marcus Li: noted. also to clarify rollout strategies: we support canary, A/B, automatic fallback to smaller model, and per-route configuration in the Console.
[00:08:15] Sofia Patel: Onboarding logistics: Elena will be the CSM and primary contact for scheduling weekly syncs; we typically do twice-weekly for the first two weeks.
[00:08:26] Elena Gomez: yes i'll set up the first three weekly sessions in the calendar after this call.
[00:08:32] Carlos Rivera: perfect.
[00:08:35] Jill Thompson: one more question — how do you handle PII scrubbing for logs and telemetry?
[00:08:40] Marcus Li: we provide redaction hooks and can redact PII before persisting logs; also customers can configure not to persist request/response bodies at all.
[00:08:50] Linda Park: we'll want to see the list of fields you capture in logs and retention controls.
[00:08:55] Marcus Li: i'll include that in the security doc.
[00:09:00] Sofia Patel: ok i want to recap and assign owners.
[00:09:05] Sofia Patel: Recap: send runbook & SSO docs (Sofia), sample prompts and success metrics (Acme by 10/17), benchmark plan & run (Marcus by 10/20), security questions list (Linda by 10/18), Elena to schedule weekly onboarding sessions.
[00:09:20] Rajesh Kumar: sounds good.
[00:09:23] Jill Thompson: thanks everyone.
[00:09:26] Sofia Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the doc and links in the next 24 hours.
[00:09:31] Elena Gomez: I'll send calendar invites and shared drive links.
[00:09:35] Carlos Rivera: thanks, bye.
[00:09:37] Linda Park: bye.

[00:09:40] End of recording (transcription incomplete after 09:40 mark due to automated segmentation)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings and brief overlaps; some product names may be abbreviated or slightly off (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed as 'k v cache' at times).

References shared: onboarding runbook link (will be shared via email), compliance pack (link to be provided post-NDA), sample benchmark spreadsheet (Marcus to create).

Explicit next steps / deliverables: see action_items above.
